method: profile-specific dispositions with hard gates; no universal score

use_cases: shared web and native component model
constraints: team accepts ecosystem assembly
accessibility and performance budgets are enforced

rationale: The documented component model fits stateful product interfaces and leaves architecture choices outside the UI library.
hard_gates: Prototype the highest-interaction screen and measure accessibility, hydration, bundle, and maintenance costs.
Choose routing, data, rendering, and deployment layers explicitly rather than treating React as a complete stack.
assessments.verification_gap: Extract a current candidate-specific independent adoption or retention signal and audit the selected framework/toolchain versions before commitment.

use_cases: React web application with server rendering
integrated web frontend and server routes
constraints: deployment target supports required runtime features
team accepts framework release cadence and rendering model

rationale: The documented integrated surface can reduce initial assembly work when React, routing, rendering, and server behavior belong in one application boundary.
hard_gates: Run the representative deployment adapter and cache behavior in the intended hosting environment.
Verify data, authentication, observability, and rollback behavior under production-like rendering paths.
assessments.verification_gap: No seed evidence compares current operational complexity, upgrade burden, or hosting portability against the other full-stack candidates.

constraints: team wants a progressive adoption path
full-stack concerns can remain separate

rationale: The documented progressive adoption model supports introducing components without requiring a complete application-framework commitment.
hard_gates: Prototype integration with the existing build, type, test, and server-rendering environment.
Confirm team familiarity and library support for required UI and accessibility primitives.
assessments.verification_gap: The seed snapshot has no candidate-specific independent maintenance, hiring, or ecosystem-retention extract.

constraints: Vue is already selected
target hosting has a verified Nuxt adapter

rationale: Nuxt's documented routing, rendering, server, module, and adapter surface can consolidate a Vue application boundary.
hard_gates: Verify the intended adapter, cache behavior, server routes, and failure recovery on the target host.
Review module provenance and pin only the modules required by the product.
assessments.verification_gap: No seed evidence compares current module maintenance, upgrade burden, or deployment portability against other full-stack frameworks.

constraints: team accepts compile-time framework semantics
required component integrations are verified

rationale: The documented compiled component model is a coherent option for testing a concise UI implementation without assuming universal performance benefits.
hard_gates: Build a representative interaction and measure generated output, accessibility, debugging, and test ergonomics.
Verify availability and maintenance of required UI integrations.
assessments.verification_gap: The seed snapshot lacks a candidate-specific independent retention, ecosystem coverage, and production-maintenance extract.

constraints: target adapter is supported
team accepts Svelte and SvelteKit release semantics

rationale: The documented routing, data, forms, endpoints, rendering, and adapter model offers a bounded way to test a Svelte full-stack product.
hard_gates: Run the application on the actual hosting adapter and verify request, cache, authentication, and rollback behavior.
Measure accessibility, bundle, server, and upgrade costs on a representative vertical slice.
assessments.verification_gap: No seed evidence compares current hosting portability, ecosystem depth, or upgrade burden against Nuxt and Next.js.

use_cases: documentation or marketing surface with bounded interactivity
constraints: most pages do not require application-wide client state
content and build pipelines fit the deployment target

rationale: Astro's documented content-oriented, server-first, opt-in-interactivity model aligns with pages where client JavaScript should be deliberate.
hard_gates: Confirm that interaction requirements remain island-shaped rather than application-shell shaped.
Validate content collections, localization, preview, build time, and deployment behavior on representative content.
assessments.verification_gap: The seed snapshot has no candidate-specific independent operational or ecosystem-retention extract.

constraints: Python is a product constraint
the team owns validation, persistence, security, and operations choices

rationale: The type-hint and generated OpenAPI surface supports a fast vertical-slice test for a Python service interface.
hard_gates: Load-test the real sync and async dependency path rather than a synthetic hello-world route.
Verify authentication, validation, persistence, migrations, error contracts, telemetry, and deployment ownership.
assessments.verification_gap: A current candidate-specific maintenance, security, dependency, and production-operations signal has not been extracted.

constraints: Python is acceptable
integrated ORM and administration are product leverage rather than unwanted coupling

rationale: Django's documented integrated data, administration, security, and deployment surface can reduce assembly work for conventional data-backed products.
hard_gates: Model the hardest schema, permission, background-work, and API boundary before adopting the integrated stack.
Run Django's deployment and security checks and define an upgrade policy for supported releases.
assessments.verification_gap: The seed snapshot lacks a current candidate-specific dependency health, hiring, upgrade, and workload-fit signal.

constraints: JVM skills and runtime are already supported
the team benefits from integrated operations and ecosystem conventions

rationale: The documented production configuration, packaging, endpoint, and operations surface aligns with teams that already operate JVM services.
hard_gates: Verify supported Java, dependency, container, startup, memory, and observability behavior in the target platform.
Constrain auto-configuration and dependency scope with architecture tests and an upgrade plan.
assessments.verification_gap: No current candidate-specific comparison of operational cost, upgrade load, staffing, or dependency risk was extracted.

use_cases: relational queries with evolving application data
constraints: relational consistency is useful
operations or a managed service are budgeted

rationale: The documented transactional, concurrency, indexing, replication, and extensibility surface covers many system-of-record requirements without assuming one hosting model.
hard_gates: Prototype the hardest transaction and query shapes using representative data volume and concurrency.
Define backup, restore, migration, high-availability, capacity, and managed-service exit procedures.
assessments.verification_gap: The seed snapshot has no workload-specific benchmark, managed-provider assessment, current vulnerability scan, or dependency-health receipt.

use_cases: high-throughput event integration or stream processing
constraints: replay and partitioned ordering are explicit requirements
the team can own or buy cluster operations

rationale: Kafka's documented partitioned, replicated log and producer, consumer, and stream APIs match requirements that truly need replayable multi-consumer streams.
hard_gates: Prove that a database outbox, managed queue, or batch pipeline cannot satisfy the same requirement more simply.
Run failure, rebalance, schema-evolution, retention, recovery, and cost tests with production-shaped traffic.
assessments.verification_gap: The independent evidence is landscape context only; no current candidate-specific operations, security, or comparative workload signal was extracted.

use_cases: shared declarative deployment and operations control plane
constraints: service and team scale justifies a platform
platform engineering or a managed control plane is funded

rationale: Kubernetes' documented declarative APIs and controllers are relevant when a shared orchestration control plane is itself a justified platform requirement.
hard_gates: Demonstrate why a simpler managed application or container service does not satisfy the reliability and deployment needs.
Budget platform ownership, upgrades, policy, networking, secrets, observability, incident response, and workload portability.
assessments.verification_gap: The lifecycle evidence supplies governance method but this seed does not record a current project-stage receipt, security posture, provider comparison, or team-operability test.

use_cases: shared telemetry collection and semantic conventions
constraints: multiple services or backends justify standardization
signal and language maturity are verified

rationale: The documented vendor-neutral APIs, SDKs, protocol, semantics, and collector create a plausible interoperability boundary for distributed observability.
hard_gates: Verify every required language, signal, instrumentation library, semantic convention, collector component, and backend exporter at current versions.
Measure telemetry loss, cardinality, sampling, cost, privacy, and failure behavior under representative load.
assessments.verification_gap: The seed snapshot does not record component-by-component stability or a target-backend compatibility test.

constraints: a separate database server is unnecessary
write contention and independent scaling are bounded

rationale: SQLite's documented embedded, file-backed transactional model removes a server boundary where locality and operational simplicity dominate.
hard_gates: Test the actual concurrency, locking, durability, backup, migration, and file-lifecycle behavior on every target platform.
Define the threshold and migration path for moving to a service database if multi-writer or independent-scale needs appear.
assessments.verification_gap: The seed snapshot has no workload-specific concurrency benchmark, binding assessment, or target-platform filesystem test.

constraints: local process execution is allowed
arguments, streams, exit codes, and artifacts form a stable contract

rationale: A narrow process boundary can be directly exercised by people, scripts, CI, and agents while retaining inspectable arguments, output, and exit status.
hard_gates: Specify non-interactive behavior, structured output, exit codes, timeouts, idempotency, secret handling, and platform support.
Test quoting, encoding, paths, cancellation, partial failure, and large output on every supported operating system.
assessments.verification_gap: POSIX utility syntax does not establish a complete cross-platform process contract, Windows behavior, discovery, or security model.

constraints: network service ownership is justified
identity, schemas, lifecycle, reliability, and observability are explicit

rationale: Standard HTTP semantics provide a broad interoperable base when the capability must be remote and serve multiple client implementations.
hard_gates: Define and test authentication, authorization, schemas, idempotency, pagination, errors, versioning, rate limits, retries, timeouts, and deprecation.
Run threat modeling, privacy, load, failure, and compatibility tests against the real client and deployment paths.
assessments.verification_gap: RFC 9110 is only the transport semantics layer; the target API contract and operational evidence remain unspecified.

use_cases: typed in-process access to one provider
constraints: the exact provider, language, package, version, license, and support policy must be named

rationale: Native SDK integration is too provider-specific to assess as one durable candidate; typed ergonomics and vendor coupling must be evaluated on the concrete package.
hard_gates: Name the exact SDK and collect first-party API, versioning, support, authentication, and license evidence.
Test error behavior, retries, timeouts, transport escape hatches, dependency impact, and upgrade compatibility.
assessments.verification_gap: There is deliberately no first-party evidence until a concrete SDK is supplied.

constraints: the host supports the required MCP revision
the server can run locally with least privilege

rationale: The revisioned MCP contract adds structured capability and tool discovery to a local client-managed process boundary.
hard_gates: Verify host and server protocol-version compatibility, process lifecycle, cancellation, timeouts, schema behavior, and log separation.
Review server provenance and permissions, isolate secrets and filesystem/network access, and test failure recovery.
assessments.verification_gap: Ecosystem activity does not verify the trust, quality, installation state, or usefulness of any particular server.

constraints: multiple remote clients justify service ownership
identity, authorization, tenancy, and audit controls are funded

rationale: The revisioned MCP HTTP transport can preserve protocol-level tool discovery for a capability that genuinely must be remote.
hard_gates: Verify protocol revision, authorization, origin and network controls, session behavior, tenancy, audit, rate limits, timeouts, retries, and revocation.
Test at least one target client end to end and treat registry metadata as discovery only.
assessments.verification_gap: The registry is preview discovery metadata and supplies no trust, health, data-residency, or client-interoperability proof for a target server.

use_cases: lazy-loaded instructions with bundled deterministic helpers
constraints: the capability is guidance or local workflow rather than a network service
each target host is tested

rationale: The documented package structure and progressive disclosure model keep routing metadata compact while allowing deeper instructions, references, scripts, and assets to load only when selected.
hard_gates: Test trigger precision, negative routing, token cost, path conventions, scripts, and failure behavior on every target host.
Keep runtime inventory, credentials, and mutable provider state outside the skill package.
assessments.verification_gap: The seed evidence proves one host implementation but not conformance or identical allowed-tools and discovery behavior across Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and future hosts.
